items.title: James Moody interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: I was on tour with Brook Benton. The Brook Benton Revue, with Ruth Brown, the Falcons, and the James Moody Orchestra.

ctx.x: Improvising really. When you heard Lester Young, and you heard Charlie Barnet, and as you said there wasn’t schools to do at that time, how did you go about learning how to play jazz?

Listening to records. I’d hear something and then try to play it like I thought maybe it sounded. And that’s how I did. And I played by ear for the longest time. And Tom McIntosh is the one that showed me changes you see? And that’s why I’ll always be indebted to him, man. I was on tour with Brook Benton. The Brook Benton Revue, with Ruth Brown, the Falcons, and the James Moody Orchestra. Okay? This was on the bus. And we get finished playing, I had that septet. I had the “Moody’s Mood for Love” thing, so I had…
So up until that point, even when you recorded “Moody’s Mood for Love,” it was all coming from your ear.
